prompt:
Create a Roblox game called Echofall.
Genre: Multiplayer Adventure, Exploration, Survival and Social Strategy.
The map is a massive floating world made of islands connected by bridges, caves, forests, snowy mountains, volcanoes, deserts and ancient ruins.
Every new server starts with the exact same peaceful world.
Hidden in the game is an invisible system called "The Echo."
Every player action adds points to different Echo categories:
• Fighting increases Chaos. • Building increases Civilization. • Exploring increases Discovery. • Helping players increases Harmony. • Destroying nature increases Corruption.
Every five minutes, whichever category is strongest permanently changes the server.
Examples:
Chaos creates stronger monsters, meteor showers and dangerous weather.
Harmony creates healing springs, friendly creatures and safe villages.
Civilization causes NPCs to build towns, roads and trading posts.
Discovery reveals secret caves, floating islands and hidden bosses.
Corruption slowly transforms forests into dark biomes with unique loot.
None of these events are announced beforehand. Players only notice the world changing around them.
Every server develops differently depending on its players.
Add over 150 random world events.
Examples include:
Giant walking castles.
Dragon migrations.
Ancient doors opening.
Floating whales flying through the sky.
Eclipse events.
Treasure storms.
Underground kingdoms appearing.
Living forests.
Crystal rain.
Giant sea monsters.
Every event should be rare and unpredictable.
Players begin with nothing.
Progress by crafting equipment, discovering recipes, unlocking abilities, collecting pets and earning Echo powers.
Instead of traditional levels, players gain Reputation from exploration, teamwork and achievements.
Reputation unlocks cosmetics, titles, mounts and emotes instead of stronger weapons.
Hidden around the world are mysterious Echo Relics.
When enough relics are activated together, the entire server enters a unique Endgame State.
There should be at least 20 different Endgame States, each completely transforming the world.
Examples:
Eternal Night.
Sky Kingdom.
Frozen World.
Machine Civilization.
Ocean Planet.
Monster Dominion.
Ancient Gods Return.
Every Endgame State has exclusive bosses, loot, music, weather and visual effects.
Add dynamic music that changes depending on the world's condition.
Include day/night cycles, realistic weather, seasons and natural disasters.
Create highly detailed environments with vibrant lighting, particles and cinematic effects.
Design every creature with unique behaviours instead of simple attacks.
NPCs should remember player actions and react differently based on reputation.
Add hidden puzzles requiring multiple players to solve together.
Include thousands of collectible items, hundreds of armour sets, rare mounts, pets, emotes, titles and visual cosmetics.
Keep all gameplay fair with no pay-to-win mechanics.
Monetisation should only include cosmetics, pets, visual effects, animations, emotes and premium housing decorations.
Optimise the game for mobile, console and PC with smooth performance.
The goal is to create a world where every server tells a completely different story, encouraging players to return because they never know what adventure will happen next.

prompt:
Subway Surfers-Style Endless Runner - Game Mechanics Spec
Core Concept
Third-person endless runner. Player character auto-runs forward along a train track corridor, dodging obstacles and collecting coins. Run ends on collision. Score scales with distance and coins.

World Layout
Lane System
 • 3 parallel lanes, each 8 studs wide, centered at X = -8, 0, +8
 • Player snaps between lanes with a 0.15s lerp (not instant teleport)
 • Track runs along +Z axis infinitely
Chunk Streaming
 • World built from prefab "chunks" 100 studs long
 • Keep 6 chunks loaded ahead of player, 2 behind
 • Spawn new chunk when player crosses a chunk boundary, destroy chunks >200 studs behind
 • Chunk pool: reuse instances rather than Instance.new each time
 • Chunk types: Empty, TrainYard, BarrierRun, TunnelSection, RampSection
 • Weighted random selection, no repeating the same chunk type twice in a row

Player Movement
Forward Speed
 • Base: 40 studs/sec
 • Increases by 1.5 studs/sec every 15 seconds
 • Hard cap: 110 studs/sec
 • Player is moved via a script setting position each frame (CFrame lerp or BodyVelocity on a HumanoidRootPart), not by Humanoid:Move - control must be scripted, not physics-driven

Movement Rules
 • Lane change is blocked if already at outermost lane
 • Lane change during jump is allowed (air control)
 • Roll cancels a jump early (fast-fall)
 • Jump cannot be buffered mid-air (no double jump unless powerup active)
 • Input buffer window: 0.12s before landing, queued input executes on land
Swipe Detection (Mobile)
 • Register swipe if touch delta > 40 pixels within 0.3s
 • Dominant axis determines direction

Generation Rules (critical - spec this clearly for the AI builder)
 • Never generate an obstacle set that blocks all 3 lanes with no valid action
 • Minimum 25 studs of clear space between obstacle groups at base speed; scale this gap up proportionally with current speed
 • Moving trains only spawn in chunks flagged safe (adjacent lanes clear for 60 studs)
 • Difficulty tiers by distance: 0-500m easy (max 1 lane blocked), 500-1500m medium (max 2 lanes blocked), 1500m+ hard (2 lanes blocked, faster trains, tighter gaps)

Collectibles
Coins
 • Spawn in arcs, straight lines of 5-10, or in curves that trace jump arcs
 • Value: 1 coin = 1 currency, 1 currency = 10 score points
 • Rotate 90°/sec on Y axis for visual polish
 • Collected via distance check (< 3 studs) not touch events - touch events are unreliable at high speed
 • Play pickup sound and small particle burst
Powerups (spawn ~1 per 300 studs, weighted)

 • Powerup pickups do not stack duration; re-picking refreshes timer to full
 • Multiple different powerups can be active simultaneously
 • Active powerup shown as HUD icon with a radial countdown

Collision & Death
Hitbox
 • Player hitbox: 4 x 6 x 4 studs, attached to root part
 • During roll: 4 x 3 x 4, offset down
 • Use Region3 or OverlapParams spatial query each frame against an Obstacles CollectionService tag, not .Touched
Death Sequence
 1 Freeze forward movement
 2 Play stumble/impact animation and sound
 3 Camera pulls back over 0.5s
 4 Show Game Over UI after 1s delay
Near-Miss Bonus
 • If player passes within 2 studs of an obstacle without collision, award 5 bonus points and flash a "Close Call!" text

Scoring
Score = floor(DistanceInStuds) + (CoinsCollected × 10) + NearMissBonus
Final Score = Score × ActiveMultiplier
 • Display live score in HUD, updating every frame
 • Track high score per player, save via DataStore
 • Coins persist across runs as a spendable currency

Camera
 • Third-person, positioned behind and above player
 • Offset: (0, 12, -18) relative to player, looking at a point 10 studs ahead of player
 • Lerp camera position at alpha 0.15 per frame for smoothing - do not hard-attach
 • FOV: 70 base, lerps to 85 at max speed for speed sensation
 • Slight camera shake on lane change (0.3 stud amplitude, 0.1s)
 • Set Camera.CameraType = Enum.CameraType.Scriptable

UI
In-Run HUD
 • Top-left: coin count with icon
 • Top-center: current score
 • Top-right: current multiplier
 • Below score: active powerup icons with countdown rings
 • Mobile: no on-screen buttons, swipe only
Game Over Screen
 • Final score, high score, coins earned this run
 • "Play Again" and "Shop" buttons
 • If new high score, show a "New Record!" banner
Shop
 • Character skins (cosmetic only, no gameplay effect)
 • Permanent upgrades: starting powerup duration +1s per level, max 5 levels each
 • Purchasable revive (costs coins, resumes run from a safe position 20 studs back)

Audio

 • SFX: jump, land, roll, coin pickup (pitch rises with combo), powerup pickup, crash, near-miss whoosh
 • Duck music volume 50% during death sequence

Technical Notes for Roblox Implementation
 • All gameplay logic client-side for responsiveness; server validates final score before DataStore write
 • Use RunService.RenderStepped for camera, Heartbeat for movement and collision
 • Tag all obstacles with CollectionService tag Obstacle, coins with Coin, powerups with Powerup
 • Store chunk prefabs in ReplicatedStorage.Chunks
 • Anchor every part in chunks; set CanCollide = false on all obstacles (collision handled by spatial query)
 • Target 60 FPS: keep loaded part count under 2000, use StreamingEnabled on the Workspace
